title: Bathrooms, shared areas and resident equipment boundaries
audience: Cleaners and cleaning supervisors who clean bathrooms, shared areas and resident rooms in residential aged care, clinics and NDIS settings in any Australian state or territory.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NHMRC, Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) (no page date shown); NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4 (November 2021), Core Module (no page date shown); Aged Care Quality Standards, Action 3.17 (guidance resource): reprocessing reusable equipment and devices (no date shown; 'Last updated' label with no date). Only part of each of these sources has been confirmed.
learningOutcomes: Describe the cleaning sequence for a shared bathroom, using the facility's approved method and frequency.
Identify the boundary between permitted environmental surfaces and resident equipment, including clinical devices and assistive equipment.
Respect resident privacy, dignity and personal belongings while cleaning shared and personal areas.
State the referral step for a request that crosses the equipment boundary.

instruction.heading: Why shared bathrooms need a structured method
instruction.body: A shared bathroom in residential aged care is touched by several people in a short time: handrails, taps, flush levers, toilet seats, grab rails, shower chairs and the door. It is also a place where body fluids and soil are more likely to be present, which increases the risk of spreading organisms. The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare treat cleaning with detergent as the routine base, with disinfection where indicated. A structured method keeps the sequence consistent: clear the area, clean from the cleanest to the most soiled surface, use cloths for one zone, and finish with the high-touch points. Follow the facility method for the product, the contact condition and the frequency.

instruction.heading: The sequence in a shared bathroom
instruction.body: Enter the bathroom with clean equipment and the approved products. Check the notice on the door and the list of resident equipment that must not be moved or cleaned by you. Start with the fixtures and surfaces that are least soiled, and work toward the toilet and floor. Clean the high-touch points as a set, including rails, taps, flush levers and the door handle inside and out. Use separate cloths for the toilet and the washbasin where the facility requires. Keep the floor cleaning separate from the surfaces, and remove soiled water and cloths by the designated route. Leave the bathroom in the state the schedule and the product label require.

instruction.heading: The boundary with resident equipment
instruction.body: Resident equipment includes assistive devices such as walking frames, wheelchairs, hoists, shower chairs and commodes, and clinical devices such as monitors, pumps and call systems. Some of these are part of the room's cleaning list and may be cleaned by you using the approved product. Clinical devices, and any equipment that a clinician has set up for a resident, are not cleaned by you unless the facility has authorised the task in writing. Do not move a resident's equipment to reach a surface, and do not remove a clinical lead or cable to clean around it. Where the boundary is unclear, leave the item as found and refer to the nurse or carer.

instruction.heading: Privacy, dignity and personal belongings
instruction.body: Personal belongings, medication, papers and photographs in a resident's room or bathroom are not yours to move, read or handle. Ask the resident or carer before moving a personal item to clean under it, and return it to the same place. Knock, introduce yourself and close doors while you work, and keep residents' dignity in mind when a resident is in the bathroom. If a resident asks you to stop, or appears distressed, stop that part of the task, tell the carer, and record the event. Do not continue to force access or to finish a task at the cost of a resident's comfort.

instruction.heading: Worked scenario: the monitor in the shared bathroom
instruction.body: A resident asks you to wipe the screen of a clinical monitor that is mounted in a shared bathroom, saying that it has fingerprints and that their family will be upset. The monitor is a clinical device, and the boundary is not yours to cross unless the facility has authorised that task in writing. Explain politely that the nurse will attend to it, do not touch the device, tell the carer or nurse the same moment, and record the request, the referral and the time. Continue with the rest of the bathroom using the approved method.

procedure: Check the door notice and the resident equipment list for the bathroom before starting.
Clear the area of personal items only with the resident's or carer's permission, and return items to their place.
Clean the least soiled surfaces first, then the high-touch points, then the toilet and floor, using separate cloths where required.
Leave clinical devices and resident equipment outside your list as found, and refer any request that crosses the boundary.
Remove soiled water and cloths by the designated route, and keep clean supplies separate from used items.
Record the area cleaned, the method, any boundary referral, any refused access and the time.

workedExamples.situation: A resident's commode is in a shared bathroom and soiled. The schedule lists the bathroom floor and fixtures, but not the commode.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not clean the commode unless it is on your authorised list or a written instruction covers it. Tell the carer or supervisor, leave the commode as directed, and clean the bathroom surfaces on the schedule. Record the referral and the time.

workedExamples.situation: A resident is sitting on the toilet when you arrive to clean the bathroom. The resident asks you to come back later.
workedExamples.reasoning: Leave the bathroom, close the door, and return later as the resident asks. Tell the carer or supervisor that the bathroom was postponed at the resident's request, and record the time. Do not argue or continue the task while the resident is in the room.

equipmentAndPpe: Facility approved product list for bathrooms: {{business:materials.approved_products}}
Separate cloths for toilet and washbasin, as required by the facility
Resident equipment and clinical device list for the area, provided by the facility

commonErrors.error: Cleaning a clinical device or moving a resident's assistive equipment to reach a surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave equipment outside your list as found, and refer any boundary question.

commonErrors.error: Moving a resident's personal items without asking, or leaving them out of place.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask first, move only with permission, and return items to their original place.

commonErrors.error: Using the same cloth on the toilet and the washbasin.
commonErrors.prevention: Use separate cloths for each zone as the facility requires, and set used cloths aside.

commonErrors.error: Continuing a task while a resident is in the room or has asked you to stop.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, leave the room, and return later, recording the postponement.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) recommend cleaning shared clinical equipment with detergent between patient uses and disinfecting where indicated (recommendation number not re-verified in this pass). Decisions about clinical equipment belong to the clinical team and the facility.

The Aged Care Quality Standards Action 3.17 page is a guidance resource (no date shown) on reprocessing reusable equipment and devices. It does not describe residential aged care specifically, and it is not a cleaning instruction for resident equipment. Reprocessing is outside this course.

The NDIS Practice Standards, Version 4 of November 2021, Core Module, require that workers are trained in standard precautions and that environmental cleaning is carried out in settings other than participants' homes. Resident dignity and privacy apply in every setting.

qualityStandard: The learner describes the cleaning sequence for a shared bathroom in the facility order, with separate cloths and a finish on high-touch points.
The learner identifies in three supplied items whether they are within the cleaning list or outside it, and refers the outside items.
The learner handles a supplied personal item with permission and returns it to its place.
The learner stops and postpones a room task at a resident's request, and records the postponement.
documentationEvidence: Area cleaned, method and product, and frequency applied
Any boundary referral, the item referred and the person referred to
Any refused access, postponed task or stop at a resident's request, with the time
summary: Clean a shared bathroom in the facility sequence, least soiled first, with separate cloths where required.
Clinical devices and resident equipment outside your list are left as found and referred.
Personal items are moved only with permission and returned to their place.
Stop and postpone at a resident's request, and record the event.

knowledgeChecks.question: A resident's commode is soiled, but it is not on your authorised list. What should you do?
options: Leave it as directed, tell the carer or supervisor, and clean the listed surfaces.
Clean it, since it is in the bathroom you are cleaning and it is part of the task today
Move it to the corridor so the floor can be cleaned underneath it more easily now

knowledgeChecks.question: A resident asks you to come back later while they are using the bathroom. What is the correct action?
options: Continue cleaning quietly while the resident is in the room.
Leave, close the door, return later, and record the postponement.
Ask the resident to leave the bathroom so you can finish.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about resident equipment is correct?
options: Any equipment in the room may be cleaned if it looks dirty, since the cleaner can judge that for themselves
Clinical devices are always cleaned by the cleaner at the end of the round, with the same product as the room
Clinical devices and equipment outside your list are left as found unless the facility authorises the task in writing.
